title: The ninth: Arafah
hookLine: standing on the plain from noon to sunset: Hajj is Arafah (Tirmidhi)

cards: A group of travelers arrives at the plain of Arafah and finds the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ there. They have one question: what is the Hajj? A man is sent to call out his answer to the crowd, and it's short.
The Hajj is Arafah. The report, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'mar, is in the collection of Tirmidhi. The cloths, the circling, the walking, the tents: all of it leads to this one day.

teach.b: First, the word. Wuquf means standing, and it's the name for being present on the plain of Arafah on the ninth day. You met this day from home back on day one hundred twenty-eight; today, the plain itself.
Tirmidhi's report goes on: whoever reaches Arafah before dawn after that night has caught the Hajj. Miss it, and in the teaching of the scholars the Hajj itself is missed, whatever else was done.

Second, what the Prophet did. Jabir's account in Sahih Muslim says he left Mina after sunrise, and when the sun passed its height, he addressed the people; then the noon and afternoon prayers were prayed together.
Then he rode to the place of standing, faced the qiblah, and stayed there, still on his camel, until the sun had set.
Noon to sunset: that's the shape of the day. Third, what standing means.
It doesn't require being on your feet. Pilgrims sit under umbrellas, stand by the roadside, rest in tents, lift their hands, read the Qur'an, cry, say nothing at all.
The rite is being there, turned toward God, for those hours. Fourth, why this day.
Aisha reports, in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet saying that there is no day on which Allah sets free more servants from the Fire than the day of Arafah.
So the plain fills with people asking, for themselves, for their parents, for names written on scraps of paper by people at home. At sunset the whole crowd moves at once.
Surah two gives the instruction for that moment, in Pickthall's words: "But, when ye press on in the multitude from 'Arafat, remember Allah by the sacred monument." That's where tomorrow begins.

how: On the ninth of Dhul-Hijjah, pilgrims go from Mina to the plain of Arafah, pray the noon and afternoon prayers together, and spend the afternoon until sunset in du'a, recitation and remembrance before moving on to Muzdalifah.

standing in rows behind the leader in daily prayer
being present on the plain of Arafah, noon to sunset

the Prophet stayed at the place of standing until sunset
so Jabir reports in Sahih Muslim.
Arafah is a minor stop on the way to Mecca

games.q: travelers find the Prophet at Arafah and ask what the Hajj is. what does he answer?
o: the Hajj is the circling of the House.
the Hajj is the journey itself.
games.why: the Hajj is Arafah. whoever reaches it before dawn after that night has caught the Hajj, according to the report in Tirmidhi.

practice: Stand, or sit if standing is hard, and turn your palms up; pilgrims give a whole afternoon to this, and a few minutes is a real start.
If you pray, ask in your own words for yourself and then for someone else by name; if not, hold in mind what you most hope for, and one person you hope it for too.

wordCard.voice: Wuquf. Standing on the plain of Arafah, from noon to sunset on the ninth, the heart of the Hajj. Today's word.

orig.note: standing: the name for being present at Arafah.

carryVoice: Your line: hajj is arafah. One afternoon of being there is the heart of it all. See you at Muzdalifah.

sources.q: But, when ye press on in the multitude from 'Arafat, remember Allah by the sacred monument.
